samples.text:
The chart shows the life expectancy at birth of men and women in six countries in 2022.

In every country, women live longer than men. Japan has the highest life expectancy, women 87.1 years and men 81.1 years. Spain is second with 85.9 years for women and 80.4 years for men. Chile is also quite high, 82.1 for women and 77.2 for men.

Russia is interesting because the difference between men and women is very big. Women can live 77.8 years but men only 67.0 years, so the gap is almost 11 years. In Egypt, men life expectancy is 69.5 years, which is higher than Russian men, but women is 74.1 years, which is lower than Russian women.

Kenya has the lowest life expectancy for both sex. Men is 60.2 years and women is 65.4 years, so they are much lower than the other countries.

Overall, women have longer life expectancy than men in all countries, and Japan is the highest while Kenya is the lowest.
samples.why: Figures accurate and the key Russia/Egypt contrast noted · basic overview at the end · simple linking · some informal and imprecise wording · agreement, word-form and noun-modifier errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The bar chart compares male and female life expectancy at birth in six countries in 2022.

Overall, women were expected to live longer than men in all six countries. Japan had the highest life expectancy for both sexes, whereas Kenya had the lowest, and the gap between men and women was noticeably wider in Russia than elsewhere.

Japan topped the chart, with a life expectancy of 87.1 years for women and 81.1 years for men, closely followed by Spain, where the figures were 85.9 and 80.4 years. Chile came next, with women expected to live to 82.1 and men to 77.2 years.

Russia stood out because of it's large gender gap of almost 11 years: Russian women could expect to live 77.8 years, while men could only expect 67.0 years. Interestingly, Russian men had a lower life expectancy than Egyptian men (69.5 years), even though Russian women outlived their Egyptian counterparts, whose figure was 74.1 years. Kenya recorded the lowest figures of all, with 65.4 years for women and just 60.2 years for men, around 21 years less than Japanese men.
samples.why: Clear overview of the gender gap, highest and lowest · key features highlighted with apt comparisons · good cohesion · some less common vocabulary · mostly accurate grammar with one apostrophe slip.

samples.text:
The chart shows the life expectancy at birth of men and women in six countries in 2022.

In all six countries, women could expect to outlive men, typically by five years or so. Life expectancy was highest in Japan and lowest in Kenya for both sexes, while Russia was unusual in having a gender gap roughly twice as large as those elsewhere.

Japan and Spain had the highest figures, with Japanese women expected to live to 87.1 and men to 81.1, and the equivalent Spanish figures only slightly lower, at 85.9 and 80.4. Chile followed, at 82.1 years for women and 77.2 for men. At the other end of the scale, Kenyan men had a life expectancy of just 60.2 years, more than 20 years below that of Japanese men, and Kenyan women 65.4.

The most striking feature, however, was the disparity in Russia. There, women could expect to reach 77.8 years, but men only 67.0, a difference of 10.8 years. In fact, Russian men had a lower life expectancy than men in Egypt (69.5), even though Russian women lived considerably longer than Egyptian women, whose figure was 74.1. Egypt, in turn, had the smallest gender gap on the chart, at 4.6 years.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected, including an insightful cross-country contrast · clear overview · accurate derived gaps · cohesion managed well · precise, varied vocabulary · complex sentences handled without error.
